correctness.rationale: With time multiplied by mu, the discovery hazards are u and v and the departure hazard is z; the successful waiting-service hazards are 1/2 and 1 by Poisson thinning, including when z=0. Inverting the transient generator independently gives T times mu equal to the stated mean. The cleared derivative numerator has leading coefficient 4(u-v)>0, linear coefficient 4L and constant -P. For P>0 the roots have opposite signs, so F decreases then increases across the unique positive root; its limiting value at infinity cannot be a better optimum. For P<=0, L=2vu^2-P>0, so F increases strictly at every positive z, even at P=0 where the endpoint derivative vanishes. The discriminant of P as a quadratic in u is 1-2v-7v^2; its unique positive zero is v_c, and for v<=v_c the vertex (1-v)/(4v) is above v since 1-v-4v^2>=v+3v^2>0. Together with P(v,v)=v^2(2v+1)>0 this places the two distinct roots, or the double root, in u>v. Substitution certifies the radical examples and the zero window at v=1/4. The result is confined to a time-homogeneous abandonment rate in the conditioned reduced chain.
residual_risks: No statement about the unconditioned whole colony, spatially resolved search, or optimization over state-dependent or time-dependent abandonment policies is implied.

value.rationale: This is the smallest conditional setting in which one individual both helps discovery and takes service opportunities from the last hungry recipient. The strict finite–zero–finite optimum classification and exact collision threshold give a benchmark that an observation of a numerical intermediate optimum for a large colony does not supply. Optimizing the reduced chain is mathematically useful without claiming a biologically prescriptive residence time.
residual_risks: Memoryless arrival and departure, fixed service rate and the conditioned initial state are substantive; extreme rates may violate the motivating spatial approximation.
